personality_voice.book_baseline: Across all seven books, Dumbledore's voice is defined by: calm authority under pressure, dry and self-aware wit deployed as a social instrument, strategic obliqueness (hinting rather than telling), measured speech rich with qualification and subordinate clauses, emotional warmth expressed through understatement, philosophical depth, and rare but powerful breaks in composure. His humor ranges from gentle whimsy (lemon drops, vulture hats, chamber pot anecdotes) to sharp irony ('Impaled upon your own sword, Gilderoy'). His defining register is one of controlled revelation - he says difficult things gently, withholds deliberately, and signals honesty while concealing. In OotP and DH especially, a private anguished register emerges: tears, buried face in hands, the King's Cross vulnerability. In HBP and GoF, intellectual impatience and cold disappointment are visible secondary traits. The full voice is layered, not reducible to warmth and wisdom alone.
personality_voice.film_portrayal: The films preserve the dominant surface traits consistently across all six films covered: composed authority, gentle wit, oblique guidance, calm defiance of institutional pressure. Key verbal signatures survive intact in multiple films (CoS: 'It is our choices'; PoA: 'How extraordinary'; HBP: 'I am with you'; DH: 'Words are our most inexhaustible source of magic'). The King's Cross scene in DH2 is the strongest piece of vocal faithfulness in the corpus - vulnerability, self-reproach, and elliptical explanation all present. The PoA hospital wing and HBP cave sequence are also vocally faithful. Harris's PS/CoS Dumbledore is warm and measured. Gambon's Dumbledore preserves the core but introduces variation in register.
personality_voice.difference: The GoF Goblet scene is the single most documented vocal contradiction: the film substitutes shouting and physical grabbing for the book's explicitly noted calm. The systematic loss of ironic-digressive humour across GoF (chamber pot anecdote, Aberforth-goat story, troll joke) removes the primary texture of his wit in that book. The private emotional register - tears in OotP, face-buried-in-hands - is largely absent from the films. The full philosophical speeches (OotP confession, HBP Horcrux theory, DH King's Cross self-accounting) are all compressed. The intellectual impatience and cold disappointment of HBP are absent. DH loses the sustained pattern of evasion as a character trait. PoA and HBP each add slightly more sentimental film-original lines not quite in his register. Across the series the film voice is recognisably his but softer, less sardonic, and more conventionally wise.
personality_voice.penalty_logic: The dominant traits survive across all films and no film fundamentally mischaracterises his voice. The GoF contradiction is the most serious single failure. The cumulative loss of secondary texture - the ironic-digressive humour, the private emotional register, the philosophical depth, the impatience - is significant but distributed rather than concentrated. Weighted toward the most important books for his voice (GoF, OotP, DH, HBP), the per-book scores (20, 17, 18, 18, 21, 18, 20) average to approximately 18.9. The GoF deviation and cumulative texture loss justify landing at 19.

narrative_role_agency.book_baseline: Dumbledore is the primary plot architect across the series. In PS he designs the Stone's protections and engineers Harry's path. In CoS he is investigator, advocate, and post-crisis arbiter. In PoA he is the time-turner architect and moral reframer. In GoF he is covert strategist, Order mobiliser, and the structural fulcrum of the revelation plot. In OotP he is the procedural defender, emergency responder, duellist, and confessor who reveals the prophecy. In HBP he is the Horcrux hunter, intellectual curriculum designer, and self-sacrificing mission leader. In DH he is the absent architect whose planning drives almost every plot mechanism. His agency is consistently the hidden engine of the narrative.
narrative_role_agency.film_portrayal: Plot-mechanical agency is well preserved across all films: PS (Stone protection, hospital wing explainer), CoS (investigator, advocate, Dobby enabler), PoA (time-turner architect, crisis manager), OotP (hearing defender, emergency responder, duellist), HBP (Horcrux strategist, cave mission leader), DH (Pensieve director, King's Cross explainer). Crisis-response and institutional-authority functions are consistently intact. The films generally preserve the scenes where his agency is most visually obvious.
narrative_role_agency.difference: The most significant agency losses are: (1) GoF - the entire proactive strategic layer is removed (Sirius correspondence, Order mobilisation, five-point action plan to Fudge), making him reactive rather than directive; (2) OotP - the prophecy revelation is partly transferred to the orb itself, removing his role as contextualiser of the series' central truth; (3) HBP - the full Pensieve curriculum is compressed from multiple lessons to two, removing his extended intellectual guidance role; (4) DH - much of the investigative function for Dumbledore's past is given to Hermione rather than being Harry's active reckoning. The closing moral guidance conversations with Harry (PoA, PS) that are his most active moments of narrative agency for Harry's psychological development are absent from PoA and compressed in PS.
narrative_role_agency.penalty_logic: Per-book scores (14, 13, 16, 17, 15, 17, 14) average to approximately 15.1. The GoF and OotP agency losses are the most significant structural failures. The consistent preservation of crisis-response and institutional functions prevents a lower score. The pattern of losing the proactive/strategic layer while preserving the reactive/visible layer is consistent across the series. Score: 15.

motivations_internal_conflict.book_baseline: Dumbledore's motivations evolve across the series from relatively opaque (PS/CoS) to explicitly complex (OotP/DH). Core motivations throughout: protecting Harry and the innocent, preparing Harry for the inevitable confrontation, operating within institutional constraints he finds inadequate, trusting people others reject (Lupin, Snape, Hagrid). Deepening across the series: guilt over Ariana's death, guilt over contributing to Sirius's imprisonment, awareness of his own capacity for self-deception (the Grindelwald friendship), his lifelong decision not to take power because he knows he cannot be trusted with it, his instrumentalisation of Harry balanced against genuine love, and his most complex internal conflict in OotP - that love as a motive became a strategic error ('I acted exactly as Voldemort expects we fools who love to act').
motivations_internal_conflict.film_portrayal: The surface motivations are consistently preserved: protect Harry, prepare him, act within constraints, trust the unconventional. The films correctly identify what Dumbledore wants. The OotP film preserves the distance-as-protection logic. The DH films preserve the guilt over Ariana and the recognition of his Grindelwald-era selfishness. The HBP film preserves the urgency around mortality and Horcruxes.
motivations_internal_conflict.difference: The internal conflict dimension is consistently simplified across all films. OotP loses the specific named tension between love-as-protection and love-as-sabotage. DH loses the full weight of the Grindelwald ideology as his own invention and his cowardice in delaying the confrontation. HBP loses the guilt about Sirius and the self-aware fallibility. PoA loses the guilt about contributing to Sirius's imprisonment. GoF loses the Pensieve-as-cognitive-overload that shows him working to stay ahead rather than omnisciently knowing. The pattern across the series is: motivations are directionally correct but flattened from complex, guilty, self-aware to simply caring-and-protective.
motivations_internal_conflict.penalty_logic: Per-book scores (11, 11, 13, 12, 11, 12, 12) average to 11.7. The motivations are never inverted or replaced with wrong ones, but the internal conflict dimension - which becomes progressively more important as the series develops - is consistently underdeveloped. The pattern is uniform simplification rather than selective failure. Score: 12.

character_arc.book_baseline: Dumbledore has a deliberately flat arc within each individual book - he is the stable centre around whom others develop. Across the series, the arc is a sustained retrospective revelation: from distant symbol of safety (PS) to increasingly legible character (CoS/PoA) to the figure whose distance is revealed as a form of love and error (OotP) to the man completing a deliberate self-sacrifice (HBP) to the posthumously revealed full portrait of a flawed, guilt-driven, brilliant human being (DH). Harry's growing understanding of Dumbledore is the primary vehicle for the arc. The key arc steps that matter most are: the PoA closing conversation (reveals philosophical depth), the OotP confession (reveals culpability and love as flaw), the HBP finality (reveals acceptance of death as strategic choice), and the DH retrospective (reveals full human complexity including selfishness and cowardice).
character_arc.film_portrayal: The within-book flat arcs are consistently reproduced - the films do not invent personal transformation arcs. The across-series revelation arc is structurally preserved: Dumbledore becomes more complex as the films progress, the OotP arc from distant to confessional is present, the HBP culmination is well-executed, the DH King's Cross revelation is the strongest arc moment in the film corpus.
character_arc.difference: The most important individual arc steps are systematically compressed. The PoA closing conversation - capstone of his depth revelation - is absent. The OotP confession arrives at the right destination but without the specific steps (naming each error, connecting distance to Sirius's death, the tears). The DH disillusionment arc - Harry's sustained fury and deliberate choice to trust - is compressed, reducing the emotional weight of the King's Cross resolution. The HBP arc loses its middle development (progressive intimacy, self-examination). Each book's arc is incomplete rather than altered - the trajectory is right but important steps are skipped.
character_arc.penalty_logic: Per-book scores (13, 13, 13, 13, 13, 11, 13) average to 12.7. The flat within-book arcs are faithfully reproduced. The across-series revelation arc is present but consistently arrives at destinations with truncated journeys. The most important missing step is the OotP explicit assumption of responsibility for Sirius's death, which is the emotional climax of the series-arc for his character. Score: 12.

key_relationships.book_baseline: The relationships that define Dumbledore across the series are: (1) Harry - mentorship evolving from protective distance to near-parental warmth, with friction and frustration as important secondary textures; the relationship's repair and reckoning in OotP and DH is structurally central; (2) Snape - absolute trust maintained despite visible tension, cold leverage of Snape's love for Lily, genuine respect and regret, the full complexity revealed in DH; (3) McGonagall - mutual respect with power differential, her exasperated admiration as a vehicle for his personality in PS; (4) Hagrid - fierce, explicit, politically costly loyalty; (5) Fudge - collegial surface over deep disagreement; (6) Grindelwald - the formative relationship revealing his greatest shame and deepest vulnerability, present retrospectively in DH.
key_relationships.film_portrayal: The Hagrid loyalty is consistently well-preserved across films. The Fudge confrontation is well-preserved in OotP. The Snape relationship is faithfully rendered in the DH Pensieve scenes. The Harry relationship is present in all films with warmth and mentorial warmth intact. The Grindelwald connection is present in DH through the Skeeter book and King's Cross.
key_relationships.difference: The Harry relationship loses its defining emotional moments across multiple films: the PoA closing conversation (most explicit personal connection to James), the OotP accumulated frustration and repair arc, the HBP cold disappointment scene, the DH explicit naming of grievances. The relationship is consistently warmer and simpler in the films than in the books - the friction and the reckoning are the most significant losses. The McGonagall dynamic is substantially altered in PS by Privet Drive scene compression. The Snape relationship's full complexity is underserved in PS through GoF and only fully rendered in DH. The Grindelwald relationship's depth is compressed across DH. No relationship is fundamentally falsified but the most emotionally complex dimension of each is consistently reduced.
key_relationships.penalty_logic: Per-book scores (7, 7, 8, 7, 7, 7, 7) average to 7.1. The consistency of the 7 score across almost every book reflects a systematic pattern: relationships are structurally present but their defining emotional complexity is removed. The Harry relationship's richer moments are the most significant series-wide loss. The only clear preservation above the 7 range is CoS (8) where most dynamics are functionally intact. Score: 7.

complexity_nuance_lost_material.book_baseline: The books' Dumbledore is complex in ways that resist the 'wise benevolent mentor' archetype: he is calculating and capable of cold manipulation (using Harry as bait, raising Harry for sacrifice, leveraging Snape's love), self-aware about his own dangerous capacity for self-deception (the Grindelwald ideology, the Hallows obsession), capable of genuine guilt and grief (Ariana, Sirius, the ring moment), occasionally cold or impatient, dry and sardonic in register rather than simply warm. The gleam of triumph in GoF is the single most important nuance in the series - a moment of hidden calculation that complicates everything. Other crucial nuances: the sock deflection (PS), the Snape psychological portrait (PS), the Pensieve as cognitive overload (GoF), the Christmas feast dry humour (PoA), the OotP tears, the HBP cold disappointment, the full DH self-indictment including cowardice about the Grindelwald confrontation.
complexity_nuance_lost_material.film_portrayal: The films preserve the most structurally visible complexity: the strategic deception, the composure under pressure, the warmth toward Harry, the King's Cross vulnerability (DH), the Pensieve coldness toward Snape (DH). The Tower scene in HBP preserves psychological precision. The CoS Lucius confrontation preserves knowing opposition. These are real and meaningful preservations.
complexity_nuance_lost_material.difference: Lost across the series: the gleam of triumph (GoF - most important single nuance); the sock deflection and Snape psychological portrait (PS); the Christmas feast humour and closing conversation depth (PoA); the Pensieve-as-cognitive-overload (GoF); the OotP tears and full confession; the HBP cold disappointment and broom shed emotional directness; the DH cowardice about the Grindelwald confrontation; the sustained pattern of strategic evasion as a character trait; the full self-indictment of his youthful selfishness. The cumulative effect is a film Dumbledore who is recognisably wise and warm but from whom the most uncomfortable and most interesting edges have been systematically smoothed. He is not flattened to a single trait but the contradictions that make him extraordinary are present only in outline.
complexity_nuance_lost_material.penalty_logic: Per-book scores (9, 9, 10, 9, 8, 9, 10) average to 9.1. The pattern is uniform: the films preserve the heroic and warm dimensions while losing the edges. The gleam of triumph is the single largest individual loss. The cumulative effect of losing the private register, the calculating coldness, the self-aware fallibility, and the ironic-digressive humour across all films constitutes meaningful but not catastrophic simplification. Score: 9.

comparative.key_observations: The films' Dumbledore is a broadly faithful but systematically simplified portrait of the book character. Three patterns repeat across all six films. First, the dominant surface traits - composed authority, oblique guidance, warm wit, calm defiance - are consistently preserved, making him immediately recognisable. Second, the proactive and strategic layer is consistently reduced: the films give us a Dumbledore who responds wisely to crises; the books give us one who has been quietly engineering outcomes for months. Third, the emotional and moral complexity - the private guilt, the self-aware fallibility, the capacity for cold calculation and disappointment - is consistently smoothed into a more conventionally wise and benevolent mentor figure. The most important books for his arc are OotP (where his culpability is explicitly named) and DH (where his full human complexity is retrospectively revealed), and both suffer from the same failure: the compression of the sustained emotional journeys that give the arc its weight. The single most important lost nuance in the series is the GoF gleam of triumph, which is the one moment in the corpus that complicates his relationship with Harry beyond simple benevolence - its absence changes how the entire character reads in retrospect. The GoF Goblet scene (shouting vs. the book's explicitly noted calm) is the only outright tonal contradiction rather than omission. The total score of 74 reflects a Dumbledore who is substantially the same person in all externally observable respects but from whom the interior complexity, the most revealing conversations, and the least comfortable edges have been consistently removed.
